title: Learning Classifiers under Delayed Feedback with a Time Window Assumption

problem.claim: Delayed feedback makes binary classification difficult because initially observed negative samples may later become positive, causing naive labeling to produce a biased classifier.

gap.claim: Existing studies reported that using only samples observed beyond a time window performs poorly, while using all samples with the time window assumption improves empirical performance.

contributions.claim: A method is proposed that constructs an unbiased and convex empirical risk from all samples under the time window assumption.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experimental results on a synthetic dataset and an open real-traffic online advertising dataset are reported to demonstrate the soundness of the proposed method.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper considers binary classification with delayed feedback, where labels can change over time.
Delayed feedback occurs in applications such as online advertising and causes naive classification to be biased.
A time window assumption treats sufficiently old samples as correctly labeled, but prior work reported limitations in using only that subset.
The authors propose constructing an unbiased and convex empirical risk from all samples under the time window assumption.
The abstract reports experiments on synthetic and real online advertising traffic datasets.

source_observation.claim: Delayed feedback can cause initially negative samples to later become positive and can bias naive classifiers.

interpretation.claim: Learning systems with label maturation should account for temporal changes in observed outcomes.

application.claim: When delayed outcomes are present, consider time-window assumptions together with methods that use all available samples.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when the time window assumption is valid or how the method behaves when it is violated.

unknowns: The duration or selection procedure for the time window is unspecified.
The mathematical construction and optimization procedure for the empirical risk are unspecified.
Dataset sizes, evaluation metrics, baselines, and quantitative results are unspecified.
The abstract does not report conditions under which the time window assumption fails.
